result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.count_loops()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count self-loops grouped by node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23366-L23431){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.count_loops() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns a dictionary mapping node IDs to the count of self-loops for each node. Only includes nodes that have at least one self-loop. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping node IDs to self-loop counts. Only includes nodes with count >= 1. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - only returns nodes with at least one self-loop - a node can have multiple self-loops (all counted) - useful for identifying unusual patterns in network data - common in multigraphs where multiple self-edges may exist ## Examples {.doc-examples} Nodes can have more than one self-loop, so this groups the count by node rather than returning a flat list of edges: ::: {#74e12cfb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True) g.add_node(label="A") g.add_node(label="B") g.add_node(label="C") g.add_node(label="D") g.add_edge(source="A", target="B") g.add_edge(source="A", target="A") # Self-loop g.add_edge(source="A", target="A") # Another self-loop g.add_edge(source="B", target="B") # Self-loop g.add_edge(source="C", target="D") # No self-loop loop_counts = g.count_loops() # Returns {'A': 2, 'B': 1} {g.get_label_from_id(nid): count for nid, count in loop_counts.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'B': 1, 'A': 2} ``` ::: ::: In a chemical reaction network, this can highlight autocatalytic species -- ones that catalyze their own production through one or more self-referencing pathways: ::: {#86209de4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} rxn = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="B") # B catalyzes itself .add_edge(source="B", target="B") # Multiple pathways .add_edge(source="C", target="C") # C is autocatalytic ) autocatalytic = rxn.count_loops() # Returns {'B': 2, 'C': 1} {rxn.get_label_from_id(nid): count for nid, count in autocatalytic.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'B': 2, 'C': 1} ``` ::: :::
